lines.t: That's the Smudge's label! A minute isn't 100 seconds. One full turn of the second hand is how many seconds?
60 is for minutes and seconds. A day has its own number. How many hours make a day?
An hour is 60 minutes, not 100.
So 2 hours 10 minutes is not 210 minutes. Time trades 60 at a time!
60 is for minutes. A day has 24 hours, not 60. 24 and 6 more?
Hello, I'm Cora. A wrong clock is worse than no clock. Everybody in town is late!
Hours and minutes trade 60. Days and hours trade 24. Never 100!

lines.t: Picture the second hand going all the way around once. How many little marks did it pass?
I picture the tower clock.
Every full turn of the minute hand is 1 hour, 60 little marks. So 2 hours is 2 full turns.
Time A goes 10 marks past 2 turns. Time B goes only 5 marks past. Time A is longer!
That's the number the hand points at. Each number on a clock is 5 minutes. Count by 5s.
Count by 5s from the 12: 5, 10, 15 … one jump for each number.
1 day 6 hours isn't 106 hours. Picture the day wheel: 1 full turn is 24 hours, then 6 more.
5 h 5 min isn't 505 minutes. An hour is 60 minutes, so 5 hours is 5 groups of 60.
Hi! I'm Hazel. I'm drawing the train at the station. Look how shiny it is!
I picture the minute hand. Every full turn around the clock is 1 hour.

lines.t: 35 and 65 make 100. But a minute is 60 seconds, not 100. Count up from 35 to 60.
Count up from 35 to 60: 40, 50, 60 … How many did you count?
My way is all minutes.
I change Time A to minutes. 2 hours is 2 × 60, so 120 minutes. And 10 more makes 130 minutes.
Time B is 125 minutes. 130 − 125 = 5.
Time A is longer by 5 minutes. Same answer as Atlas!
1 day is 24 hours. Now add the 6 extra hours.
Change the day first: 1 day is 24 hours. Then add the 6 extra hours.
5 × 60 = 300 minutes for the hours. Now add the 5 extra minutes.
Change the hours first: 5 × 60 minutes. Then add the 5 extra minutes.
Hey, I'm Felix! I heard the big clock tick once, and then nothing. Something is stuck in there.
Going down, I multiply. 5 hours is 5 × 60, so 300 minutes. Add 15 more: 315 minutes.

lines.t: Look at the day wheel words on your page: how many hours make a day?
My way is hours and minutes.
I wind Time B's 125 minutes and count the full turns: 60, 120. That's 2 hours, and 5 minutes are left.
So Time B is 2 hours 5 minutes. Time A is 2 hours 10 minutes.
Both are 2 hours, and 10 minutes is 5 more than 5 minutes. Time A is longer by 5 minutes!
Hi, I'm Atlas! Look how tall the Clock Tower is. I bet you can see Hilltop from the top!
Going up, I count full hours. 145 minutes is two 60s and 25 more, so 2 hours 25 minutes.

lines.t: Hoo! Welcome to the Clock Tower, {name}. Last time you rebuilt the Gallon-Man, and the trough showed GOLEM PART 1.
The Smudge is building something, and this clock can tell us when it comes. But listen. No ticking!
That's Otto, the clockkeeper, by the tower. Go say hello.
Hoo! The Math Crew solved the stopped-clock puzzle. They each found the answer their own way.
Hoo! Two ways, and one answer: Time A is longer by 5 minutes.
Thirty hours until the Golem comes. Next time, the night market, {name}.
Hoo! Every tower job on the page helps Otto get his clock running.
Hoo! Thirty hours is plenty of time, {name}.
Next lesson, the night market. The Smudge's factory has to be somewhere nearby.

lines.t: Oh! A visitor. I'm Otto, keeper of the Clock Tower.
The Smudge stopped my clock and smudged the numbers on its face. I can't read the time!
Walk up to the tower and read where the minute hand points. Each number on a clock is 5 minutes.
My clock ticks, but the hands still skip!
The Smudge threw three gears out of the tower and smudged their labels. Please find them and fix them. Walk onto a sparkle to pick one up.
Every gear is back in place. Thank you, {name}!
Now the hands turn smoothly. Come back when the timetable is ready.
Here is the new timetable for the station.
Please take it to the station master, by the train.
The timetable is right, and my clock keeps perfect time again.
Listen! It's about to chime for the first time since the Smudge came. Stand by the tower.
Welcome to the Clock Tower! Seconds, minutes, hours and days. I keep them all.
You did it! My clock is running again.
Thank you, {name}. Now let's get the rest of the tower fixed.
